# GOALS

## Problem and the end result from the user's point of view

Generation always writes all four public Go files, even when a binding has
nothing to put in one. Twelve tracked files in this repository are the generated
header comment and a `package` clause and nothing else:

    // Code generated by zigo. DO NOT EDIT.
    package scalar

A user opening `scalar_type_gen.go` after generating bindings finds an empty
file and has to work out whether generation failed. Afterwards those files are
simply not created.

## Measurable goals

- No generated `.go` file consists only of the marker comment and the `package`
  clause.
- The twelve such files under `examples/` and `tests/generator_cases/` are gone,
  and regeneration does not recreate them.
- Regenerating over a tree that has one from an earlier run removes it, so
  `zigo check` does not then report it as obsolete.

## Supported scope and non-goals

In scope: `src/gen/generator.zig`'s commit loop, the tests that assert the
empty files exist, and the generated artifacts checked into the repository.

Not in scope: the non-Go outputs. `shim.zig`, `panic.c`, the C header, and
`errors.lock.json` are always meaningful and are always written. Also not in
scope: pruning generated files whose *path* changed for another reason — the
existing `zigo check` obsolete report already covers that, and deleting outside
the paths this run owns is a different, riskier decision.

## Reference source / commit / license

None.

## Completion criteria for the whole plan

`zig build test` and `zig build check` pass, no tracked generated `.go` file is
declaration-free, and a regeneration test proves the stale-file removal.
